newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine C.Bank presents policy independence bill.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine C.Bank presents policy independence bill.

text.p: Ukraine's central bank has presented to parliament a bill which would limit influence on bank policy by elected officials to a new consulting board, the bank's chairman told a news conference on Saturday.
"The National Bank of Ukraine's leaders have forwarded a bill which presupposes the independence of the central bank in administering monetary policy," Viktor Yushchenko said.
In recent weeks Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko said he planned to head a special commission to oversee central bank activities, and the bank said such a move would be illegal.
Yushchenko said the proposed law would limit direct influence on bank policy to a consulting body on which the president and members of parliament could serve.

"This would be exclusively a consulting body, whose goal would be to make recommendations. The central bank would be in charge of monetary policy and would be responsible for the end results," he said.
But a member of parliament's commission on banking activities, Vadim Hetman, said the central bank bill would give the consulting body a veto -- a limited one -- on bank policy.

"We want to give the bank the ability to surmount this veto by giving it a two-thirds vote (on the consulting board), to let it take full responsibility for key decisions and activities," he told Reuters.
He said parliament likely would hold the first reading for the draft law and decide whether to support Yushchenko to continue as central bank chairman at the end of January.

"I don't see any alternative to the National Bank of Ukraine chairman we have today, because the (economic) stability we've had this year was in large part thanks to the bank's monetary policies," he said.
